rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies an expanded/thinned-zona blastocyst and appropriately notes likely post-handling collapse and limited image quality. ICM/TE descriptions are cautious and broadly consistent with the reported 3AA, though the image alone does not allow a highly precise AA-level assessment.
Strong integration of age, ovarian reserve, BMI, male-factor diagnosis, semen parameters, prior biochemical pregnancy, endometrium, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with prognosis tied to embryo grade and favorable patient factors. Minor issue: some overinterpretation of endometrial thickness/OHSS context and broad probability framing, but overall coherent.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice: reliance on lab grading, elective single embryo transfer in a young patient, no routine PGT-A after one biochemical, and avoidance of bed rest. Slightly speculative comments about thick endometrium/OHSS prevent a perfect score.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support confirmation, alcohol cessation, prenatal care, and when to escalate evaluation. Useful, though some recommendations remain somewhat general rather than protocol-specific.
